name: inkscape-hidden-state-layers-quiz
exporter: Inkscape 1.3 - File > Save As... > Inkscape SVG
story: A school quiz board drawn the way docs/SVG_AUTHORING.md §5b asks for: the base look, then one layer per moment with the eye clicked off - and Inkscape writes an eye clicked off as style="display:none" on the layer itself.
idioms: hidden layers as style="display:none" in the element's own style attribute - Inkscape's shape for an eye clicked off, where the corpus previously had only Illustrator's class="st12" plus a .st12{display:none} rule
one layer switched off as style="visibility:hidden" instead, which is what editing the attribute in Inkscape's XML editor leaves behind
two of the hidden layers carry <text> of their own ("LOCKED IN", "+1") - drawn states with words in them, not just tinted rectangles
nested <g inkscape:groupmode="layer"> sublayers inside the drawing layer, each with inkscape:label and a hand-typed id
inkscape:label on the <text> elements as well as on the layers, with serial-free hand-typed ids
typography entirely in style="" (font-size:52px;font-family:Archivo;-inkscape-font-specification:'Archivo Bold'), zero presentation attributes
xml:space="preserve" on every <text> with <tspan sodipodi:role="line"> repeating the parent's x/y and no whitespace between the tags
the answer WORDS placed last in document order, under nothing - §5b's z-order advice followed
one attribute per line at a 3-space continuation indent, self-closing tags written as ' />'
Finnish sample copy with a non-ASCII character (Mikä)
whyThisMatters: The quiz is one of the two graphics the 2026-09-12 production is decided by, and §5b's whole instruction to the student is "hide those layers in your design app" - so which hiding IDIOMS are understood is load-bearing, not a detail. The corpus proved exactly one of them: Illustrator's class rule. Inkscape is the free tool a school actually installs, it writes the inline-style form instead, and two of these hidden layers carry words. If the inline form is missed, the board arrives with seven text fields instead of five and two of them type into a stamp nobody can see - and the operator would find that out on air. The visibility:hidden layer covers the other half of the same test, which no fixture reached at all.
